data.title: Moisturisers & emollients (Aquasoft, Physiogel-type, ceramide creams)
data.summary: VI Keratolytics & emollients · Barrier repair agents: occlusives, humectants, emollients and physiological lipids
data.body:
_Topicals · VI Keratolytics & emollients_

**Class:** Barrier repair agents: occlusives, humectants, emollients and physiological lipids

## Mechanism of action
- Occlusives (petrolatum, mineral oil, dimethicone, lanolin) form a film that reduces transepidermal water loss (TEWL); petrolatum is the most effective
- Humectants (glycerin, urea, lactic acid, hyaluronic acid, propylene glycol) draw water into the stratum corneum
- Emollients (fatty esters, plant oils, ceramides) fill gaps between corneocytes → smooth, soft skin
- Physiological lipid mixtures (ceramides : cholesterol : free fatty acids in about 3:1:1 ratio) repair the lamellar barrier in atopic skin (low ceramides)
- Physiogel AI-type creams add palmitoylethanolamide (PEA) — an anti-inflammatory/antipruritic lipid
- Aquasoft (glycerin–paraffin based cream) is a humectant–occlusive moisturiser commonly used in India

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Atopic dermatitis (cornerstone of treatment; proactive use reduces flares and steroid need)
- Ichthyoses, xerosis, asteatotic eczema in the elderly, hand eczema, psoriasis (adjunct)
- Barrier recovery with retinoid/isotretinoin therapy, after procedures
- Infant skin care (early emollient use may lower AD risk in high-risk infants — conflicting data)

## Dose & formulations
- Apply liberally and often (at least twice daily), within 3 min after bathing ('soak and seal')
- Adults may need 250–500 g per week for widespread disease; children 150–250 g per week
- Apply in the direction of hair growth (avoid folliculitis); apply 15–30 min apart from topical steroid

## Adverse effects
- Folliculitis (occlusive ointments), acneiform eruption on face
- Stinging (urea, lactic acid, propylene glycol)
- Contact allergy to fragrance, lanolin, preservatives (parabens, methylisothiazolinone)
- Fire risk: paraffin-soaked clothing/dressings near flames

## Contraindications
- Known allergy to an ingredient

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe.

## Viva points
- Occlusive vs humectant vs emollient — give examples
- Ceramide : cholesterol : FFA = 3:1:1
- Soak-and-seal within 3 min of bathing
- Paraffin-based emollients are a fire hazard

## Note on sources
Aquasoft and Physiogel are brand names; the post explains the ingredient types they represent.

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.57 (Miscellaneous topical agents — moisturisers); Khopkar ch.27 (Moisturizers). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
